title: Understanding Pipe Bellies in Drainage Systems
description: A belly or sag in a horizontal drainage line occurs when soil settling, improper hanger spacing, or thermal expansion causes a section of pipe to dip below its proper slope. This low point holds standing water, catching suspended solids, grease, and paper waste instead of letting gravity carry them away. Over time, organic debris settles inside the dip, causing chronic blockages and slow drainage. As waste decomposes in the standing water, foul odors can also develop. Ensuring firm bedding, correct slope, and proper pipe support prevents bellies and maintains continuous gravity flow.

Understanding Pipe Bellies in Drainage Systems

A belly or sag in a horizontal drainage line occurs when soil settling, improper hanger spacing, or thermal expansion causes a section of pipe to dip below its proper slope. This low point holds standing water, catching suspended solids, grease, and paper waste instead of letting gravity carry them away. Over time, organic debris settles inside the dip, causing chronic blockages and slow drainage. As waste decomposes in the standing water, foul odors can also develop. Ensuring firm bedding, correct slope, and proper pipe support prevents bellies and maintains continuous gravity flow.
